review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes of its own, and the proofs use simp/simpa only in a few places (zero_smul, smul_mem, add_left, add_right, starConvex_zero_iff). I found no competing rules, no unwanted expansion and no loop risk. The one point I found is that the `starConvex_singleton` simp lemma is missing, even though the analogous `convex_singleton` in Convex/Basic.lean is simp. I checked uses with Grep. `starConvex_singleton` is not used elsewhere in Mathlib, so the evidence for the change is parity only and the finding is low-confidence. I did not recommend simp on `starConvex_empty` or `starConvex_univ`, because the matching `convex_empty` and `convex_univ` are not simp either.

findings.excerpt: theorem starConvex_singleton (x : E) : StarConvex 𝕜 x {x} := by
findings.problem: The sibling statement `convex_singleton` is tagged @[simp]. `StarConvex 𝕜 x {x}` is the same kind of unconditional fact, and its goal has the same shape. It is not simp, so `simp` cannot close side goals of the form `StarConvex 𝕜 x {x}`, even though it can close `Convex 𝕜 {x}`. The statement is a closed True-valued fact with no hypotheses. The LHS head is the `StarConvex` constant, so a rewrite to True cannot loop or expand terms. The other nearby facts, `starConvex_empty` and `starConvex_univ`, are not simp in the Convex file either (`convex_empty` and `convex_univ` have no @[simp]), so this is the only one with a parity argument.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp] theorem starConvex_singleton (x : E) : StarConvex 𝕜 x {x}`. If maintainers prefer to avoid new simp lemmas, leave it as is. The case for the attribute rests only on parity with `convex_singleton`.
findings.benefit: `simp` could discharge star-convexity side goals for singletons, as it already does for convexity of singletons. That makes the StarConvex and Convex simp interfaces consistent.
